facts.text: Cash generation is strong but flattered by timing. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest challenge is that the improvement may not last. Reported EBITDA for Q3 2026 was USD 310.1 million against USD 219.0 million a year earlier, and FY2025 reported EBITDA of USD 845.6 million was below FY2024's USD 912.1 million, so earnings move with the semiconductor cycle. Working-capital timing and low capital expenditure also help cash flow, and cash was flat at USD 356.5 million because all excess cash went to repaying USD 450.0 million of debt rather than to liquidity. The view would change if quarterly EBITDA fell back toward the FY2025 level, if nine-month capital expenditure caught up with the USD 250.0 million plan, or if the credit agreement showed letters of credit encumbering the revolver or a covenant trigger close to current usage. limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- Medium: letters of credit drawn on the revolver are not stated for any balance sheet date, so undrawn committed facilities and liquidity may be overstated; obtain the credit agreement or a compliance statement. - Medium: the level of revolver use that triggers the first lien net leverage test of 5.20 to 1.00 is not stated, so covenant headroom is not worked out; obtain the credit agreement. - Medium: guarantors, collateral and the rank among the secured instruments are not supplied, so the debt stack ranking follows the filings' own labels; obtain the indentures and credit agreement. - Medium: the issuer states no unadjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is derived from operating income plus depreciation and amortization; the adjusted measure is shown beside it for every ratio. - Low: the 10-K does not date the revolver commitment at 2024-12-31, so undrawn facilities for that date are not supplied. - Low: carrying values by instrument are not disclosed, so the debt instruments table states principal and one financing cost adjustment row of 34.4; a floor on the revolver is not stated. - Low: the filing prints a dash for years with no maturity; the ladder shows zero for those years because the stated principal equals the sum of the other years. - Low: the dividend amount payable on 2026-11-18 is estimated from the per-share rate and shares outstanding at 2026-10-26, because the total is not stated. - Low: maintenance and growth capital expenditure are not split, and cash interest paid for the third quarter alone is not stated. - Low: the filings mention no supplier finance or receivables factoring programme, so the only non-debt funding float read is customer contract liabilities. - Low: several 10-K note tables are captioned in thousands but print millions; they are read as millions, as the 10-Q states.

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a benign view is that the demand recovery is recent and concentrated. Nine-month net sales grew 13.8% and Q3 grew 24.6%, but customers can cancel orders, the top ten customers account for half of sales and equipment-linked sales grew 42.0%, so a reversal of fab capital spending would hit revenue and the margin gains together. A second challenge is that the Low governance level rests on absence of evidence: without the proxy statement or the debt documents, a large holder, wide restricted-payment baskets or a priming right cannot be excluded. The view would change if the proxy statement named a holder with board control, if the credit agreement showed broad capacity to pay dividends or move assets outside the creditor group, if net sales fell back while capital expenditure caught up with the plan, or if further finance leadership or disclosure lapses followed. Basis: calculation C-11; calculation C-12; calculation C-16; calculation C-29; 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 10

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest challenge to a solid view is that leverage and coverage are measured near a cyclical high. Last-twelve-months reported EBITDA of USD 982.1 million is 16.1% above FY2025's USD 845.6 million and Q3 2026 net sales grew 24.6%, so the ratios flatter the through-the-cycle position. If reported EBITDA fell back to the FY2025 level, net debt at 2026-09-26 would be 3.43x EBITDA and cash interest cover 4.67x: still below the FY2025 net leverage of 3.95x, but with less room to refinance USD 2,400.0 million due in 2028 and 2029 on terms that are not yet known. The view would weaken if quarterly net sales fell below the low end of the fourth-quarter 2026 guidance of USD 1,025 million, if capital expenditure caught up with the plan and free cash flow conversion fell from 62.7%, or if the credit agreement showed a restrictive covenant trigger or broad distribution capacity; it would strengthen if the 2028 notes were refinanced early, more debt were repaid, or ratings and market prices showed open access. facts.text: Rivalry is real but the company states that no global competitor matches its full range: named competitors include Pall Corporation, part of Danaher, and the EMD Performance Materials division of Merck KGaA, so pricing power is limited to specified-in products. facts.label: Macro, policy and technology factors
facts.text: Trade policy and technology cycles are material to credit quality. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The initiating condition is a pause in fab capital spending or a customer inventory correction. The first operating break is orders cut or deferred, because customers typically give no long-term purchase commitments, which lowers volume and plant utilisation and reverses the margin gains. EBITDA would fall toward the FY2025 level; on that illustration net leverage would be 3.43x and cash interest cover 4.67x, with liquidity of USD 1,106.5 million, no maturity before 2028 and management levers in capital expenditure and the dividend, so a liquidity shortfall is not indicated. The refinancing consequence arrives later: the 2028 and 2029 maturities would be refinanced from a trough in earnings, so the observable triggers are net sales below guidance, free cash flow conversion falling, and any revolver draw. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Entegris presents an adequate business profile supported by specified-in consumable products and a deleveraging financial policy, but credit quality is constrained by customer concentration, cyclical demand and a 2029 maturity wall. Cash-flow durability appears adequate: free cash flow conversion is high but flattered by timing. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on market access in 2028 and 2029 and on earnings holding near the current level. The primary downside path is a fall in capital-spending-linked demand that cuts EBITDA before the notes are refinanced. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement and indentures, agency ratings and market prices. Top risk: refinancing the 2029 maturity from lower earnings. ## Request

## Findings
### Bottom line

The supplied Entegris filings and releases support the requested financial, business and fundamental credit work through the quarter ended 2026-09-26, but covenant, lien and recovery questions stay open because no executed debt documents were supplied.

Creditors can read the debt stack, maturity ladder, liquidity and the reported covenant compliance statement from the latest quarterly filing, whose balance sheet date is 40 days before the as-of date. The annual report's note tables are captioned in thousands although their figures are in millions, as the later quarterly filings state, so those tables need unit care. Ratings, market prices, peer data, the executed credit agreement and indentures, and the level of revolver use that switches the covenant test on are not established.

spans.text: # CP-1 Financial foundation: ENTEGRIS INC (entg), as of 2026-11-05
## Request

ENTEGRIS INC (entg), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. This module extracts and normalises the consolidated financial statements, debt, liquidity and credit metrics of Entegris, Inc. from the supplied filings and releases, for the requested financial foundation.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended 2025-12-31 | 2026-02-10 (signature date stated in the document; the third-quarter 2026 10-Q states filing on 2026-02-11) | 260dc4cc98d7ad114dcfe1b4d9e49beac9ed9f7c97f27f59e6df3a75c0628528 | FY2024 and FY2025 statements, FY2025 debt note, non-GAAP bridge, cash requirements, covenant risk factor |

| 10-Q_2026-06-27_entg-20260627.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-27 | 2026-08-04 (signature date) | 5d06fd99ce42692b479a85d0b3d96bd08dbc1bdd295141cd5adf69b1988058ed | Q2 2026 balance sheet, debt note, amended revolver terms, voluntary payment event |

| EX-99.1_2026-04-30_entgq12026ex991.htm.jsonl | Press release (Exhibit 99.1) reporting first-quarter 2026 results | 2026-04-30 | 0e10b62e7e542aab19ae90b6d94252e94c7183b272237a1b5ecd040e7a3bb9d7 | Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 stand-alone quarters |

| EX-99.1_2026-08-04_entgq22026ex991.htm.jsonl | Press release (Exhibit 99.1) reporting second-quarter 2026 results | 2026-08-04 | 729b6288fa7f91f06fa1d1330da9031db0436138ba5a59730b16535055ac78c0 | Q2 2026 stand-alone quarter |

- Source readiness (CP-0): sha256 ba3a775d3800350778736b10ab6b6cdeb19ade0b14b26c4f98e86059e9de2e38
## Findings
### Bottom line

Entegris has delevered materially: net debt is 2.96x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA, down from 3.95x at FY2025, and interest cover is 5.42x, so the creditor risk that remains is the USD 2,000.0 million of principal due in 2029, not liquidity or coverage.
Basis: calculation C-37; calculation C-31; calculation C-38; calculation C-46; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 11

Net debt at 2026-09-26 is USD 2,904.1 million (USD 2,919.38 million pro forma for the dividend payable on 2026-11-18), on total debt of USD 3,260.6 million at carrying value. Reported EBITDA is a derived figure because the issuer states only an adjusted one; on the adjusted measure net leverage is 2.88x. The 10-K note tables are captioned in thousands but print millions.
Basis: calculation C-12; calculation C-53; calculation C-40; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9
### Key findings

Leverage fell because the company repaid USD 450.0 million of term loan in 2026 while last-twelve-months reported EBITDA rose to USD 982.1 million from USD 845.6 million at FY2025. Total debt over reported EBITDA is now 3.32x against 4.37x at FY2025, and on the issuer's adjusted measure 3.23x against 4.17x. Both the repayment and the earnings recovery contributed; the repayment is permanent, while the earnings recovery depends on semiconductor demand.

Basis: calculation C-44; calculation C-36; calculation C-30; calculation C-39; calculation C-33; calculation C-14; calculation C-02; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 12

Coverage is comfortable: reported EBITDA covers cash interest 5.42x, up from 4.56x at FY2025, on last-twelve-months cash interest paid of USD 181.1 million. All remaining debt is fixed-rate notes because the term loan is repaid and the revolver is undrawn, so interest cost no longer moves with rates; the revolver carries a margin of 1.25% over SOFR if it is drawn.
Basis: calculation C-38; calculation C-32; calculation C-16; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 12

Cash generation is strong but flattered by timing. Nine-month operating cash flow of USD 606.0 million was 1.76x net income, and free cash flow reached USD 482.0 million against USD 262.2 million a year earlier, because capital expenditure fell by about half to USD 124.0 million from USD 241.2 million. Working capital absorbed USD 65.8 million net: a USD 320.7 million build in receivables and inventories was offset by higher payables and accruals, which include variable compensation still to be paid. Customer advances, the one non-debt funding source in the filings, rose to USD 74.1 million from USD 49.9 million at year-end, which is small against operating cash flow. With the 10-K planning about USD 250.0 million of 2026 capital expenditure, nine-month spending is well below plan, so this free cash flow should not be annualised.

Basis: calculation C-47; calculation C-22; calculation C-23; calculation C-48; calculation C-49; calculation C-50; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 82

Liquidity is USD 1,106.5 million: cash of USD 356.5 million plus an undrawn USD 750.0 million revolver maturing in 2031, before any letters of credit, which the filings do not state. Nothing matures before 2028; USD 400.0 million falls due in 2028, USD 2,000.0 million, or 60.7% of principal, in 2029 and USD 895.0 million in 2030. A year of free cash flow at the last-twelve-months level of USD 616.0 million would cover the 2028 maturity but not the 2029 principal, so creditors depend on refinancing access in 2028 and 2029 rather than on cash on hand.
Basis: calculation C-45; calculation C-46; calculation C-43; calculation C-19; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12

The structure puts USD 1,600.0 million of senior secured notes and the undrawn revolver ahead of three unsecured note series. Secured debt is 1.63x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA and all principal is 3.36x. Guarantors, collateral and the rank among the secured instruments are not supplied, so the ranking follows the filings' own labels.
Basis: calculation C-56; calculation C-55; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 12

The statements are consolidated for Entegris, Inc. and its subsidiaries, with no finance subsidiary to separate. Debt excludes lease liabilities of USD 100.4 million, which the balance sheet shows on their own line. Depreciation fell by USD 55.6 million over nine months after the January 2026 useful-life change, which lifts operating income and net income but not EBITDA, and Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA excludes USD 8.3 million of tariff refunds.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest challenge is that the improvement may not last. Reported EBITDA for Q3 2026 was USD 310.1 million against USD 219.0 million a year earlier, and FY2025 reported EBITDA of USD 845.6 million was below FY2024's USD 912.1 million, so earnings move with the semiconductor cycle. Working-capital timing and low capital expenditure also help cash flow, and cash was flat at USD 356.5 million because all excess cash went to repaying USD 450.0 million of debt rather than to liquidity. The view would change if quarterly EBITDA fell back toward the FY2025 level, if nine-month capital expenditure caught up with the USD 250.0 million plan, or if the credit agreement showed letters of credit encumbering the revolver or a covenant trigger close to current usage.

Basis: calculation C-06; calculation C-05; calculation C-02; calculation C-01; calculation C-44; calculation C-50; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 34
### Limitations

- Reported EBITDA is derived here from operating income plus depreciation and amortization of intangible assets, because the issuer states only an adjusted figure; a ratio on another EBITDA definition would differ, and the adjusted twin is shown beside it for that reason.
Basis: calculation C-14; calculation C-51; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 38

- Availability under the revolver net of letters of credit, the revolver covenant's trigger level, and guarantor and collateral terms are not stated in the filings, so liquidity may be slightly overstated, covenant headroom is not worked out and the ranking among secured debt follows the filings' labels.

spans.text: # CP-1A Business & governance: ENTEGRIS INC (entg), as of 2026-11-05
## Request

ENTEGRIS INC (entg), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. This module sets out the business, transaction, ownership, operating-model and governance facts of Entegris, Inc. that matter to a creditor, from the supplied filings and releases.
## Sources

| EX-99.1_2026-08-04_entgq22026ex991.htm.jsonl | Press release (Exhibit 99.1) reporting second-quarter 2026 results | 2026-08-04 | 729b6288fa7f91f06fa1d1330da9031db0436138ba5a59730b16535055ac78c0 | Q2 2026 results context |

- Source readiness (CP-0): sha256 ba3a775d3800350778736b10ab6b6cdeb19ade0b14b26c4f98e86059e9de2e38
## Findings
### Bottom line

Entegris is a semiconductor consumables supplier whose creditor risk is demand cyclicality and customer concentration, not governance: no sponsor or controlling holder is identified and the company is repaying debt rather than distributing cash.
Basis: calculation C-30; 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 95

The top ten customers were 50% of FY2025 net sales, and nine-month 2026 growth of 13.8% is led by Equipment and Engineering customers at 42.0%, the most cyclical category. Governance risk is Low but provisional, because the proxy statement, the credit agreement and the indentures were not supplied; finance leadership changed during 2026 and three insider trading plans were omitted from earlier disclosure.

Basis: calculation C-11; calculation C-16; 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 89–90; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Key findings

The business is a consumables supplier tied to semiconductor volumes, which makes earnings cyclical but less so than an equipment maker. Management describes revenue as predominantly unit-driven or recurring, and Advanced Purity Solutions, the larger segment at 58.4% of segment sales, earns 67.6% of segment profit at a 31.4% margin against 21.1% for Materials Solutions. Growth of 13.8% over nine months and 24.6% in Q3 came mainly from volume, which added USD 341.2 million over nine months, but customers give no long-term purchase commitments, so the recovery can reverse as quickly as it came.

Basis: calculation C-03; calculation C-07; calculation C-10; calculation C-09; calculation C-11; calculation C-12; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 18

Customer and regional concentration is the main business risk. The top ten customers were 50% of FY2025 net sales, up from 43% in 2023, with TSMC at 16%; Taiwan, the largest region, was 26% of nine-month 2026 sales, while China, at 18%, was flat and is exposed to trade restrictions. Equipment and Engineering customers grew 42.0% against 10.2% for fabs, so the growth is skewed to capital-spending-linked demand, which falls first in a downturn.
Basis: calculation C-16; calculation C-18; 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, pages 23–24

Governance risk is Low but provisional. No sponsor, parent or controlling holder is named in the documents supplied, and the documented behaviour is creditor-aligned: USD 450.0 million of term loan repaid in nine months 2026 from USD 606.0 million of operating cash flow, no share repurchase programme, and a quarterly dividend of USD 0.10 per share that absorbed 8.8% of FY2025 operating cash flow. Ownership and board detail sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied, and legal capacity for distributions, investments or priming cannot be assessed without the credit agreement and indentures, so the level cannot be firmer than Low.

Basis: calculation C-30; calculation C-27; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 65–66; 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 95; Source readiness (CP-0)

Finance leadership and disclosure controls are the monitoring points. The Chief Financial Officer position moved from a separation agreement on 2026-01-19, through an interim officer from 2026-03-01, to a new officer who signed the second-quarter report on 2026-08-04, while the revolver was being refinanced; three insider trading plans entered in the first quarter of 2025 were omitted from earlier disclosure through an administrative oversight, which the company says it has corrected. Neither is a financial misstatement and reporting has been regular, but they bear on the quality of lender reporting if stress returns.

Financial policy is deleveraging, and no new debt was issued in 2025 or in 2026 to date. The revolver was upsized by USD 175.0 million to USD 750.0 million and extended to 2031-04-29, removing a 2027 maturity, while the 2023 and 2024 divestitures, including USD 675.3 million for Electronic Chemicals and USD 263.2 million gross for PIM, left a simpler group. Nine-month capital expenditure of USD 124.0 million is 49.6% of the USD 250.0 million 2026 plan, so part of the cash available for debt repayment is timing.
Basis: calculation C-33; calculation C-29; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 82

Supply, trade and the accounting estimate are the other operating risks. Certain filtration and chemical inputs come from a single source or limited suppliers, tariffs and export controls remain a stated risk with China sales flat, and the January 2026 useful-life change cut nine-month depreciation by USD 55.6 million, which lifts operating income and net income but not EBITDA, so margin gains at the operating income level overstate the cash improvement.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a benign view is that the demand recovery is recent and concentrated. Nine-month net sales grew 13.8% and Q3 grew 24.6%, but customers can cancel orders, the top ten customers account for half of sales and equipment-linked sales grew 42.0%, so a reversal of fab capital spending would hit revenue and the margin gains together. A second challenge is that the Low governance level rests on absence of evidence: without the proxy statement or the debt documents, a large holder, wide restricted-payment baskets or a priming right cannot be excluded. The view would change if the proxy statement named a holder with board control, if the credit agreement showed broad capacity to pay dividends or move assets outside the creditor group, if net sales fell back while capital expenditure caught up with the plan, or if further finance leadership or disclosure lapses followed.
Basis: calculation C-11; calculation C-12; calculation C-16; calculation C-29; 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 10
### Limitations

- The Low governance level and the finding that no controlling holder exists rest on documents that name no holder; the proxy statement with beneficial ownership and board detail was not supplied, so a large holder or a board-control arrangement would raise the level.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 95

- The conclusion that distributions are not a creditor risk rests on observed behaviour only; without the credit agreement and indentures the restricted-payment, investment, priming and asset-transfer capacity is not established, and wide capacity would weaken it.
- The customer concentration conclusion uses FY2025 figures, because the quarterly filings name no customers; the current top ten share could be higher or lower than 50%.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 18

spans.text: # CP-2 Fundamental credit: ENTEGRIS INC (entg), as of 2026-11-05
## Request

ENTEGRIS INC (entg), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. This module synthesises the financial, business and governance work on Entegris, Inc. into a fundamental credit view, with its strongest support, its weakest dimension, its primary downside path and the signals to monitor.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended 2025-12-31 | 2026-02-10 (signature date stated in the document; the third-quarter 2026 10-Q states filing on 2026-02-11) | 260dc4cc98d7ad114dcfe1b4d9e49beac9ed9f7c97f27f59e6df3a75c0628528 | Business, competition, supply, covenant risk factor, dividend policy, exhibit index |

| 10-Q_2026-03-28_entg-20260328.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-03-28 | 2026-04-30 (signature date) | 3b83d32b0eaaaa1280f7799359a8f16448b715b610a83c1edceec0d49387802a | Q1 2026 liquidity and revolver amendment event |

| 10-Q_2026-06-27_entg-20260627.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-27 | 2026-08-04 (signature date) | 5d06fd99ce42692b479a85d0b3d96bd08dbc1bdd295141cd5adf69b1988058ed | Q2 2026 liquidity and debt events |

| EX-99.1_2026-08-04_entgq22026ex991.htm.jsonl | Press release (Exhibit 99.1) reporting second-quarter 2026 results | 2026-08-04 | 729b6288fa7f91f06fa1d1330da9031db0436138ba5a59730b16535055ac78c0 | Q2 2026 quarter |

| EX-99.1_2026-10-29_entgq32026ex991.htm.jsonl | Press release (Exhibit 99.1) reporting third-quarter 2026 results | 2026-10-29 | e35116403bbcb30c3a986093aa969493d265b238a073d77c0b1aa4aec9296a99 | Q3 2026 quarter and fourth-quarter guidance |
- Source readiness (CP-0): sha256 ba3a775d3800350778736b10ab6b6cdeb19ade0b14b26c4f98e86059e9de2e38
- Financial foundation (CP-1): sha256 8d07d18b2ba6fabaef828bc24d8cf3f74af5ebb6f7411ef4a5763b716bd591c5
- Business & governance (CP-1A): sha256 5a28c00ad23dcbe0e2314a1885d954f7fcfb63f30cac7f6976fcaec5fd33298c
## Findings
### Bottom line

Entegris presents a solid fundamental credit profile: net leverage of 2.96x and cash interest cover of 5.42x leave room for a downturn, but a cyclical, concentrated revenue base and USD 2,000.0 million due in 2029 mean creditors depend on market access.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-12; calculation C-15; calculation C-23

Net debt is USD 2,904.1 million at 2026-09-26, or USD 2,919.38 million pro forma for the dividend payable on 2026-11-18. The primary downside path is a fall in capital-spending-linked demand that cuts EBITDA before the 2028 and 2029 refinancing windows; last-twelve-months free cash flow of USD 616.0 million and liquidity of USD 1,106.5 million would absorb a first-year shock, but not the 2029 principal.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-07; calculation C-08; calculation C-18; calculation C-22; calculation C-33
### Key findings

Leverage and coverage are the strongest support. Net debt over reported EBITDA fell to 2.96x from 3.95x at FY2025 and total debt over reported EBITDA to 3.32x from 4.37x, because USD 450.0 million of term loan was repaid while last-twelve-months reported EBITDA rose to USD 982.1 million from USD 845.6 million; cash interest cover rose to 5.42x from 4.56x. Net leverage is 2.88x on the issuer's adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,008.2 million. All remaining debt is fixed-rate notes, so coverage now moves with earnings, not with rates.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-12; calculation C-13; calculation C-10; calculation C-11; calculation C-21; calculation C-01; calculation C-02; calculation C-15; calculation C-16; calculation C-14; calculation C-04

Cash flow is good but should not be annualised. Free cash flow of USD 616.0 million over the last twelve months is 62.7% of reported EBITDA and 18.9% of total debt, and nine-month free cash flow was USD 482.0 million against USD 262.2 million a year earlier. Capital expenditure is only 49.6% of the 2026 plan and working capital absorbed USD 65.8 million net, with receivables and inventories building while payables and accruals rose on the timing of vendor payments and higher incentive compensation accruals, so part of the improvement may reverse as spending and payments normalise.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-18; calculation C-31; calculation C-32; calculation C-19; calculation C-20; calculation C-25; calculation C-24; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 33

Liquidity is adequate and the 2029 maturity wall is the weakest dimension. Cash of USD 356.5 million and an undrawn USD 750.0 million revolver maturing in 2031 give USD 1,106.5 million, with letters of credit under the revolver not stated; nothing falls due before 2028, but 12.1% of principal is due in 2028, 60.7% in 2029 and 27.2% in 2030. The 2029 principal is 3.25 years of last-twelve-months free cash flow and liquidity covers 46.1% of the 2028 and 2029 principal, so repayment from cash alone is not the base case and refinancing access decides the outcome. The company states it has had no difficulty accessing capital markets, but no rating or market price was supplied to test that.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-22; calculation C-35; calculation C-23; calculation C-36; calculation C-33; calculation C-43; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 32

Revenue durability is average rather than strong. Management describes revenue as predominantly unit-driven or recurring and says switching away from its products is costly, but the top ten customers were 50% of FY2025 sales, customers typically give no long-term purchase commitments, and Equipment and Engineering sales, 18.3% of nine-month 2026 sales, grew 42.0% against 13.8% for total net sales. Advanced Purity Solutions earns 67.6% of segment profit, so a fall in fab capital spending would reach EBITDA through both volume and margin.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-29; calculation C-28; calculation C-30; calculation C-27; 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 10

Financial policy and governance support the view but are not locked in. No sponsor or controlling holder is named, USD 450.0 million of debt was repaid, there is no repurchase programme and the dividend took 8.8% of FY2025 operating cash flow. Legal capacity for debt, liens and distributions, the guarantor list and the proxy statement were not supplied, so a Low governance risk level is provisional and the policy rests on observed behaviour, not on documented restrictions.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-21; calculation C-26; 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 66

Structural priority and covenant questions stay open, with one refinement to Financial foundation. Financial foundation ranked the revolver and the USD 1,600.0 million of secured notes together on the filings' labels and said no rank among them was stated; the annual report's exhibit index lists an equal priority intercreditor agreement dated 2022-07-06 between the collateral agents of the senior credit facilities and of the notes, which supports equal rank but was not supplied, and names certain subsidiaries as guarantors without listing them. Unsecured notes total USD 1,695.0 million and secured notes are 48.6% of principal. The first lien net leverage covenant of 5.20x is tested only when revolver use passes an unstated threshold, and the annual report calls the test a secured net leverage ratio, so headroom is not worked out.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 96–97; 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C-37; calculation C-38
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest challenge to a solid view is that leverage and coverage are measured near a cyclical high. Last-twelve-months reported EBITDA of USD 982.1 million is 16.1% above FY2025's USD 845.6 million and Q3 2026 net sales grew 24.6%, so the ratios flatter the through-the-cycle position. If reported EBITDA fell back to the FY2025 level, net debt at 2026-09-26 would be 3.43x EBITDA and cash interest cover 4.67x: still below the FY2025 net leverage of 3.95x, but with less room to refinance USD 2,400.0 million due in 2028 and 2029 on terms that are not yet known. The view would weaken if quarterly net sales fell below the low end of the fourth-quarter 2026 guidance of USD 1,025 million, if capital expenditure caught up with the plan and free cash flow conversion fell from 62.7%, or if the credit agreement showed a restrictive covenant trigger or broad distribution capacity; it would strengthen if the 2028 notes were refinanced early, more debt were repaid, or ratings and market prices showed open access.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-01; calculation C-02; calculation C-49; calculation C-45; calculation C-39; calculation C-40; calculation C-13; calculation C-31; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_entgq32026ex991.htm.jsonl, page 2
### Limitations

- Market access for the 2028 and 2029 refinancing is judged from the revolver, the absence of reported difficulty and the company's own statement, because no agency rating, bond price or spread was supplied; a closed or expensive market would make the 2029 wall a larger weakness than shown.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 32; Source readiness (CP-0)

- The Low governance conclusion and the structural priority comment rest on filings that summarise the debt documents; the executed credit agreement and indentures could show covenant limits, guarantor scope or distribution capacity that change both.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 96–97

- The downside illustration anchors on FY2025 reported EBITDA, which is derived from operating income plus depreciation and amortization, so it shows scale and not a forecast; a deeper trough than FY2025 would raise leverage further than shown.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-39; calculation C-40
### Revenue drivers, margins and cash conversion

Revenue follows wafer volumes and fab capital spending. Volume added USD 341.2 million to nine-month 2026 net sales while currency subtracted USD 13.1 million, and the customer categories linked to equipment grew fastest. Because customers typically give no long-term purchase commitments and the top ten are half of sales, revenue is cyclical and concentrated even though products are specified into customer processes; revenue visibility rests on near-term orders, not on contracts.
Basis: calculation C-46; calculation C-28; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 18

Gross margin was 48.2% in nine months 2026 against 44.6% a year earlier, helped by volume, lower depreciation after the January 2026 useful-life change and tariff refunds, and reported EBITDA margin is 27.9% over the last twelve months. Lower depreciation lifts gross margin and operating income but not EBITDA, so the EBITDA margin gain comes from volume and plant utilisation, which reverse with demand. Cost flexibility is moderate: engineering, research and development is 9.1% of net sales and management says it will keep investing in it, while capital expenditure and the dividend are the discretionary items.

Basis: calculation C-47; calculation C-42; calculation C-48; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11

Cash conversion is high because capital expenditure is below plan and interest is falling: free cash flow is 62.7% of reported EBITDA after USD 181.1 million of cash interest, which is 5.14% of last-twelve-months net sales. Capital expenditure is the main lever in a downturn, and cutting it would protect free cash flow at the cost of slower capacity additions for new fabs.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-31; calculation C-17; calculation C-41
### Competitive forces

Rivalry is real but the company states that no global competitor matches its full range: named competitors include Pall Corporation, part of Danaher, and the EMD Performance Materials division of Merck KGaA, so pricing power is limited to specified-in products. Buyer power is high because the top ten customers are half of sales and typically give no long-term purchase commitments, which is a revenue risk, not a pricing certainty. Supplier power is moderate: certain filtration membranes, resins, abrasive particles and chemicals come from a single source or limited suppliers, and multi-year supply agreements cover part of that exposure. Threats from new entrants and substitutes are not established by the sources beyond technology transitions that management presents as an opportunity.
### Macro, policy and technology factors

Trade policy and technology cycles are material to credit quality. Tariffs and export controls are a stated cost and demand risk, China sales were flat in nine months 2026 and Taiwan is the largest region at 26% of sales; support under the CHIPS Act of up to USD 77.0 million is tied to milestones. Node transitions raise materials content per wafer, which management presents as a tailwind, but exposure to a small number of fabs means technology shifts can also move share.
### SWOT in credit terms
- Strengths: lower leverage and higher coverage after the repayment of the term loan, liquidity with no maturity before 2028, and recurring, specified-in consumables.
- Weaknesses: the 2029 maturity wall, concentrated customers without long-term purchase commitments, and free cash flow that benefits from timing.
- Opportunities that would improve credit quality: early refinancing of the 2028 notes and further voluntary repayment from free cash flow.
- Threats that would weaken it: a fall in fab capital spending, new tariffs or export controls, and a covenant or documentation constraint not yet seen.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-12; calculation C-23
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

The only guidance for the next 12 to 24 months covers the fourth quarter of 2026: net sales of USD 1,025 million to USD 1,055 million and an Adjusted EBITDA margin of 30.7% to 31.2%, which is management's view and supports near-term deleveraging if met. Tailwinds are node migration, new fab construction and a lower interest bill after the term loan repayment; headwinds are tariffs, a possible reversal in equipment-linked demand and the 2028 and 2029 maturities. No multi-year guidance is supplied, and a Capital Markets Day on 2026-11-09 falls after the as-of date and is not used.

### Downside scenario

The initiating condition is a pause in fab capital spending or a customer inventory correction. The first operating break is orders cut or deferred, because customers typically give no long-term purchase commitments, which lowers volume and plant utilisation and reverses the margin gains. EBITDA would fall toward the FY2025 level; on that illustration net leverage would be 3.43x and cash interest cover 4.67x, with liquidity of USD 1,106.5 million, no maturity before 2028 and management levers in capital expenditure and the dividend, so a liquidity shortfall is not indicated. The refinancing consequence arrives later: the 2028 and 2029 maturities would be refinanced from a trough in earnings, so the observable triggers are net sales below guidance, free cash flow conversion falling, and any revolver draw.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-39; calculation C-40; calculation C-22; calculation C-43
### Overall credit view

Overall, Entegris presents an adequate business profile supported by specified-in consumable products and a deleveraging financial policy, but credit quality is constrained by customer concentration, cyclical demand and a 2029 maturity wall. Cash-flow durability appears adequate: free cash flow conversion is high but flattered by timing. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on market access in 2028 and 2029 and on earnings holding near the current level. The primary downside path is a fall in capital-spending-linked demand that cuts EBITDA before the notes are refinanced. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement and indentures, agency ratings and market prices. Top risk: refinancing the 2029 maturity from lower earnings.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)
### Strengths and weaknesses
Strengths, ranked, each as evidence, mechanism and implication.

- Deleveraging: net debt over reported EBITDA fell to 2.96x from 3.95x as USD 450.0 million of term loan was repaid and earnings rose, which widens the cushion before leverage reaches earlier levels and removes floating-rate debt.
- Coverage: reported EBITDA covers cash interest 5.42x on fixed-rate notes, so coverage depends on earnings, and a downturn that cut EBITDA to the FY2025 level would still leave 4.67x.
- Liquidity: USD 1,106.5 million of cash and undrawn revolver, with nothing due before 2028, supports interest and working capital through a downturn of the size illustrated.
- Cash generation: last-twelve-months free cash flow of USD 616.0 million funds voluntary repayment, which is the route to a smaller 2029 refinancing.
- Financial policy: no sponsor, no repurchase programme and a dividend at 8.8% of FY2025 operating cash flow leave cash for creditors, with extraction risk low on observed behaviour.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-12; calculation C-15; calculation C-40; calculation C-22; calculation C-18; calculation C-26
Weaknesses, ranked, each as evidence, mechanism and implication.

- The 2029 maturity wall: USD 2,000.0 million, 60.7% of principal, falls due in 2029 as bullet notes, so repayment needs refinancing or 3.25 years of free cash flow, and market access becomes the deciding factor.

- Cyclical, concentrated demand: the top ten customers are 50% of sales, there are typically no long-term purchase commitments and equipment-linked sales grew fastest at 42.0%, so a capital-spending pause would hit volume and margin together.
- Free cash flow timing: capital expenditure is 49.6% of plan and accruals rose, so conversion of 62.7% may fall as spending and payments normalise.

- Unassessed legal terms: the credit agreement and indentures were not supplied, so the covenant trigger, guarantor scope and distribution capacity are not established and structural priority and recovery cannot be concluded.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-23; calculation C-33; calculation C-28; calculation C-25; calculation C-31
